=== BASH AND TOOL NOTES, RE-CONFIRMED AT CYCLE 132 ===
Bash refuses paths outside /home/runner/work/SPIRAL/SPIRAL (INCLUDING /tmp); refuses 'python3 script.py' AND 'python3 -c' (SO YOU CANNOT RUN scripts/validate_state.py -- hand-check the gates with jq, and SAY SO rather than implying a validator run); refuses 'cp'; refuses 'curl' WITHOUT APPROVAL; refuses PROCESS SUBSTITUTION '<(...)'; refuses jq's '--arg'/'--rawfile'/'--slurpfile', 'sed -i', 'for' loops, and ANY CHAINING WITH '&&' OR ';'. ONE command per Bash call. A single leading 'cd <dir>; <cmd>' IS accepted, as are 'rm -f', 'mv', redirection, 'ls', 'wc', 'head -c', 'tail', 'sed -n <range>p', 'grep -n', 'grep -c' and PIPES.
[227]: a jq program with an OBJECT CONSTRUCTOR (brace, comma, brace) is USUALLY rejected as shell brace expansion -- build an ARRAY OF LABELLED STRINGS and join it. SQUARE BRACKETS ARE SAFE. [346]: TO BUILD A NEW OBJECT IN jq WITHOUT TRIPPING BRACE EXPANSION, START FROM AN EMPTY '{}' AND ASSIGN FIELDS.
[237] THE TWO-INPUT SPLICE IS THE ONLY RELIABLE WAY TO EDIT THESE FILES: jq -n 'input as $s | input as $t | $t | <edits>' scratch.json target.json > out.json, then 'mv'. [211]/[228]: ONE scratch JSON holding EVERY new string, keyed by name, written with the Write tool; SINGLE QUOTES for all verbatim quotation so NO DOUBLE QUOTE appears in a string body -- validate the scratch with 'jq -r keys' BEFORE the splice. VERIFY WITH A COUNTS jq AND AN APPEND-ONLY-PROOF jq BEFORE THE 'mv', THEN 'rm -f' THE SCRATCH. CYCLE 132 RAN EXACTLY THIS AND IT WORKED FIRST TIME ON A TEN-KEY SCRATCH.
[347] FOR scores.json, THE FIVE-CONJUNCT APPEND-ONLY PROOF IS: keys equal; every new rationale startswith its old rationale; every new evidence array has the old one as a PREFIX; _schema unchanged; and the score vector reported explicitly, old and new side by side. NOTE THE SHAPE: scores.json's 'scores' IS AN OBJECT KEYED BY issue_id, NOT AN ARRAY -- 'jq .scores[0]' FAILS with 'Cannot index object with number'. Use '.scores|to_entries[]'.
[335] jq SCOPING TRAP: inside map(...), select(...) or [...[]|...] the '.' REBINDS to the current element. BIND THE KEY FIRST with '. as $e' and use '$e.key'.
[318] 'grep -n' on a jq-extracted field is USELESS because a whole block is ONE line; use offset slices like '.[-3200:]' or '[0:600]', or [348]'s scan() window. [348]: 'grep -o' WITH A CONTEXT-WINDOW PATTERN was REFUSED as needing approval -- use jq's scan() with a bounded window, e.g. jq '[scan("[^.]{0,260}PATTERN[^.]{0,200}")]|join("\n")', or the Grep TOOL with -C.
